name: Jolada Roti
ingredients: Small amount of wheat flour (optional, for binding)
instructions: 1. Boil water in a heavy-bottomed vessel and add a pinch of salt.
2. Gradually add sorghum flour to the boiling water, stirring continuously to form a soft dough.
3. While the dough is still warm, knead it thoroughly until smooth and pliable.
4. Take a lime-sized ball of dough and flatten it into a disc using your palms, gradually expanding it by patting.
5. Carefully transfer the roti onto a hot griddle (tava), cooked side facing up.
6. Wipe the top surface with a wet cloth to remove excess flour.
7. Flip the roti once the bottom is firm and cook until golden brown spots appear.
8. Finally, place the roti directly on an open flame to puff it up.
description: Jolada Roti is a staple unleavened flatbread from North Karnataka, synonymous with the region's rural diet. It is made from sorghum (jowar), a hardy grain well-suited to the semi-arid climate. It is culturally significant as a nutritious, fiber-rich meal typically served with spicy curries like Enne Gai (stuffed eggplant) and chutneys, forming an integral part of the local hospitality and daily sustenance.
